title: Capacitors and Capacitance Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav pulls his charger out of the wall, yet its little indicator light keeps glowing for a moment. The power is gone, so where is the energy coming from? A capacitor. In this animated lesson we build the idea from the ground up: two metal plates with an insulator, the dielectric, between them, and the symbol that shows exactly that.

On a live breadboard we charge a capacitor through a resistor: electrons pile onto one plate and leave the other, no electron crosses the gap, and the oscilloscope draws the capacitor voltage rising and levelling off. Then we flip the switch and the stored charge lights a lamp while the voltage falls away. We derive Q = CV and C = Q/V, meet the farad and its microfarad, nanofarad and picofarad, and see why bigger plates and a smaller gap give more capacitance: C = Kε₀A/d with ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F/m. A worked example finds the capacitance of a 10 cm × 10 cm plate pair 1 mm apart. Then the exam trap (voltage does not change capacitance), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 27 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 4: Passive Electronic Components (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
